reasons: The eval-case drop rule as specified cannot be implemented correctly by the design it prescribes. spec.md's Requirements and Acceptance say a case is dropped 'when nothing is left under its folder at HEAD', but spec.md's Design (and plan.md step 2) say the drop rule is 'one small pure function taking the parsed [--name-status -M diff] records ... so it is unit-testable without git'. A --name-status diff lists only files that changed between the merge base and HEAD; a file under the case folder that was never touched by the diff does not appear in those records at all, so the pure function has no way to know whether it still exists at HEAD. The consequence is concrete, not hypothetical: deleting one file out of a multi-file eval case (leaving the rest intact) would show a D under that case's path with no corresponding survivor visible to the function, and a diff-records-only implementation would have to either (a) wrongly flag the whole case as dropped (false positive park on a change that did not drop the case) or (b) under-detect real drops spread across several commits. The only way to honor the literal requirement is to also consult the tree at HEAD (e.g. git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD <folder>), which plan.md's file list for plugin/gate/diff.py does not include and which the Design explicitly says the function avoids ('without git').

This exact gap was identified by the devil's advocate on this same phase-b panel (evidence/panel/b-1-advocate.md, point 3: '--name-status records list only changed paths, so they cannot tell whether an untouched file survives under the case folder... the nearest tool at hand is the filesystem... intent.md's own Constraints and OPERATING_MODEL §3 forbid the gate to judge [the working tree]'), but the conciliator's decision (evidence/panel/b-1-conciliator.json, evidence/decisions-b.json) closes only the narrower 'framework/ is out of scope' half of the flagged concern and explicitly declines to resolve this one ('they park for the owner as their own finding rather than being folded into this concern's closure'). No such finding is actually written into spec.md's Flagged concerns, plan.md's Risks, or any Open question in this diff -- it exists only as panel-member prose, so nothing in the committed design artifacts currently tells the owner, or the build session that will read plan.md at (c), that this gap exists or how to close it.

The planned tests cannot catch this: plan.md's Order of work (step 2) builds the drop-rule's own unit tests from 'the parser from step 1 as a fixture input, not live git', i.e. synthetic parsed-record fixtures rather than a real repository at two commits. The advocate makes the same point about the one eval-case acceptance test named in plan.md's Proof ('test_ratchets_drop_eval_case_folder_emptied_fails passes either way: in a clean fixture Path.exists() and git ls-tree HEAD agree'). Acceptance as written does not include a case that distinguishes 'folder empty at HEAD' from 'some file under the folder was deleted but others remain', so an implementation with this bug would ship green.
classification_reasons: Blast radius is not small: the plan's files-that-change list reaches core gate infrastructure that runs at phases (c)/(d)/(e) for every project on the plugin (plugin/gate/checks.py, plugin/gate/diff.py, plugin/state/unpark.py, plugin/pr/description.py), plus the adversarial-reviewer agent and two templates/skills -- well above 'few files', and squarely the kind of shared enforcement code the build guide treats as elevated risk even though no sdlc.yaml risk_list item is nominally touched.

The spec is not fully tight: beyond the framework/-scope item the panel closed, this round surfaces a second, unresolved concern (the eval-case 'nothing left at HEAD' detection gap) that has no decision and no tracked requirement fix in spec.md or plan.md.

The code this plan adds is wholly new (a rename-aware diff parser, a new gate check, cross-check union logic) with no existing test coverage to lean on; every acceptance test named is a test still to be written, several of them (per the advocate's own analysis) insufficiently discriminating for the behavior they claim to prove.
attempted: Intent: re-compared intent.md's Proposed outcome against spec.md's Requirements; unchanged from the prior round and still a faithful, complete mapping (phase membership, drop rule, declared-drop exemption, risk-list-shaped hit, accept-risk reuse, skip-marker listing, reviewer/REVIEW.md angles, 'what I need from you' wording, version bump).

Spec and plan: re-read spec.md's Design and plan.md's Order of work/Proof specifically for the eval-case drop rule, since that is the one piece of this design that must infer a true/false state 'at HEAD' from a diff of changes rather than from the two full trees; found that the stated implementation approach (a pure function over parsed --name-status records, 'unit-testable without git') is structurally unable to always determine 'nothing left under its folder at HEAD', and that none of plan.md's Risks entries name this gap even though plan.md does carefully name three other, narrower risks (plan.md read source, rename-vs-two-files, union-narrowing) in the same section.

Proof: confirmed the diff at this HEAD (d3c983a) adds no source or test files beyond the previous round -- only evidence/decisions-b.json, evidence/decisions-b.md, evidence/panel/* and evidence/hook-log.jsonl/diff-b.patch bookkeeping; phase (b) remains the read-only design run, so no test.log/build.log/lint.log is expected or present, consistent with OPERATING_MODEL.

Blast radius: confirmed again that no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and no sdlc.yaml risk_list item is touched by this commit; confirmed the panel's own decision record is scoped to a narrower claim (framework/ cannot appear in the committed diff's input) than the concern as originally flagged, and that two of the three substantive points the devil's advocate raised (pin/release timing; the eval-case HEAD-detection gap) were explicitly left open by the conciliator rather than folded into a spec.md/plan.md fix.

Policies: re-checked security-baseline (argument-list git invocation, no shell=True) and data-conventions/ux-conventions scoping -- unchanged from the prior round, still correctly applied or correctly marked not-applicable.

Tests: read plan.md's Proof list against the advocate's specific claim that the named eval-case test (`test_ratchets_drop_eval_case_folder_emptied_fails`) would pass under either a correct (ls-tree-at-HEAD) or an incorrect (diff-records-only) implementation; confirmed this by tracing the Design's own description of the drop-rule function's inputs, which are limited to the parsed diff records with no HEAD-tree listing step named anywhere in Design or in plugin/gate/diff.py's planned additions.
